CAG flags expenditure irregularities in road schemes

The Comptroller and Auditor General has flagged expenditure irregularities of over Rs 400 crore in rural road schemes executed in the state over five years.

The audit report, tabled in the assembly, cites excess payments against estimates, incomplete works shown as complete, and weak third-party quality checks.

It recommends fixing responsibility on executing engineers and recovering excess payments with interest from defaulting contractors.

The rural works department said corrective action has begun and utilisation certificates are being reconciled division by division.

Opposition members demanded a time-bound probe, while the treasury benches said audit paras are routinely settled through the public accounts committee.
